# Quiet Recorder in a Storm

Version 1.20.3 takes load off Home Assistant during a thunderstorm and makes the map recover better when something goes wrong.

## Fewer requests during a storm

- **A strike no longer triggers two recorder queries.** _[#143]_ Every new strike made every open dashboard ask the recorder for the 90-day statistics and for the history chart, exactly when the recorder is busiest. The statistics are now only fetched when the card's settings change or at most every 10 minutes, and the history chart refreshes at most every 30 seconds while strikes come in. The last strike of a burst still reaches the chart.
- **The history chart shows the newest data.** _[#143]_ When two history requests overlapped, an older reply could arrive last and replace the newer data. Older replies are now ignored.

## The map

- **A map that cannot be built is no longer retried on every update.** _[#143]_ Without WebGL the map cannot start. Before, the card tried again on every state change in Home Assistant, each time requesting a token, downloading the map style and logging an error. It now tries once and only again when you change the card's settings or reload the dashboard.
- **The map keeps its tiles when a token renewal fails.** _[#143]_ When the map loads its tiles through Home Assistant's `map_tiles` proxy (the default when that integration is loaded), a failed token renewal dropped the current token, so map tiles were refused for up to 10 minutes. The card now keeps the current token and tries the renewal again after 30 seconds.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do after updating. Your configuration stays as it is. After the update, reload the dashboard so the new card file is loaded.

Requirements are unchanged: Home Assistant 2026.6 or newer.
